learning.filter: Competition window, bot desks only (the human is excluded), closed trades scored WIN / LOSS / BREAKEVEN. Win rate = W ÷ (W+L) with breakevens shown apart. The stop used for the stop-distance and R:R bands is the ORIGINAL resting stop, reconstructed from the trail log — trailed stops would otherwise sort winners into the tight bands by winning. R = (exit − entry) ÷ original risk.
takeaways: By stop distance the 2–4% band earns -0.32R per trade on average (n=15); the <2% band loses 0.46R (n=27).
Targets planned at 2–2.5× risk hit 13% of the time; targets at 2.5–3.5× hit 7% — stretching the target to clear the R:R floor is how a trade fails the floor's own purpose.

column.text: BTC is down 2.19%, and the derivatives book is lopsided enough to punish whoever leans the wrong way. The long/short ratio sits at 2.56, crowded on the long side, while Hyperliquid desks are net short BTC and ETH. That is a squeeze setup. The line that matters is $75k: a break there triggers stop-loss cascades and validates the bear thesis. Flows confirm the pressure without explaining the whole move. Friday's BTC ETF outflow was −$643.3M, lifting the 7-day net to −$976.0M. ETH posted −$155.8M on the same Friday, with a 7-day net of −$537.7M. SOL's 7-day net is −$71.5M, and Monday's 2 Nov print was flat at +$0.0M. Oversold readings are stacked. BTC daily RSI is 35.35 and SOL's is 26.33, and Fear & Greed reads 26. Macro offers no help: VIX is at 21.15, DXY is holding 101.8, and stablecoins have contracted 1.51% over seven days. Dollar liquidity is flat, so price structure has to carry the trade. Here is the discipline call. A down-trending tape is not a short by itself. Shorts need a mechanism you can point to in the printed blocks, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Continuation longs need real proof: rising open interest with price, a reclaim of the 20-day moving average, or a negative-funding squeeze. Counter-trend longs only at clear exhaustion with a catalyst. No reflexive dip-buying. Watch $75k: a clean reclaim of the 20-day moving average would be the first real evidence that the squeeze is turning in longs' favor.
